rationale: Acceptance criteria are satisfied and every Github()/GithubIntegration() constructor site now threads base_url; however two edge-case defects survive verification. (1) _normalize_github_base_url uses parsed.hostname, which strips the port — GHE instances on non-standard ports lose it and connect to 443. (2) split_git_url requires a path component; a bare Credentials.url like 'https://ghe.company.com' raises IndexError inside _build_auth_header, the bare except swallows it, and get_github_app_token falls back to api.github.com. 1 finding deferred (GITHUB_BASE_URL is a user opt-in env var, mirrors the existing GITHUB_ACCESS_TOKEN pattern) and 1 dismissed (fixture-vacuous claim, fixture does set url).

business_review.notes: github_base_url field + factories forward hostname from repo_link/GithubConfig.url; GITHUB_BASE_URL env fallback exists.
All six construction sites thread base_url — wrapper (three methods), github_client, git_auth_utils, both git_loader call sites.
_normalize_github_base_url returns https://{host}/api/v3 (no trailing slash) — verified by 14-case parametrize including trailing-slash-strip.
_get_installation_id (the ticket's line-33 method) gains base_url parameter; both GithubIntegration constructions in App-auth flow receive it.
Backward-compat asserted via 'base_url not in kwargs' for github.com across all five touched modules and both PAT+App auth paths.

standards_review.notes: No ruff violations; ruff pre-commit hook passed on final commit.
No secrets logged; URL parsing uses stdlib urlparse; env-var handling follows existing GITHUB_ACCESS_TOKEN precedent.

findings.problem: _normalize_github_base_url uses parsed.hostname, which strips any port; GHE Server on a non-standard port receives a portless base_url.
findings.impact: GHE instances listening on custom ports (e.g. https://ghe.company.com:8443) get normalized to https://ghe.company.com/api/v3 — every PyGithub call connects to port 443 instead of the real port and fails.
findings.recommendation:
Preserve the port. Change the last line of _normalize_github_base_url to something like:
    port_suffix = f':{parsed.port}' if parsed.port else ''
    return f'{scheme}://{host}{port_suffix}/api/v3'
Add a parametrize case for ('https://ghe.company.com:8443', 'https://ghe.company.com:8443/api/v3').

findings.problem: _build_auth_header calls split_git_url(creds.url); split_git_url requires a path component and raises IndexError when creds.url is a bare server URL like 'https://ghe.company.com'. The `except Exception: pass` swallows the error, leaves token_kwargs empty, and get_github_app_token defaults to api.github.com.
findings.impact: GitHub App installation token is requested from api.github.com instead of GHE; the returned token is invalid for the GHE installation and every subsequent header-authenticated git operation fails.
findings.recommendation:
Extract the hostname directly with urlparse instead of split_git_url — split_git_url is a repo-URL parser, not a base-URL parser:
    parsed_creds = urlparse(creds_url)
    hostname = (parsed_creds.hostname or '').lower()
    if hostname and hostname not in ('github.com', 'api.github.com'):
        token_kwargs['base_url'] = f'{parsed_creds.scheme}://{parsed_creds.netloc}'
Add a test with creds.url='https://ghe.company.com' (no path).
